mainTopic: The sin and punishment of the מרגלים, and the honor due to the ארון (עוזא, דוד, and בית שמש)
overview: This amud explains the פסוקים about the מרגלים one by one. רבי שמעון בן יוחי teaches that they set out with an evil plan, and רבי מאיר explains that they began with true praise so their slander would be believed. The גמרא then tells how כלב won the crowd over after יהושע was shouted down. It shows how far the מרגלים went: they claimed the Canaanites were stronger than God, and they twisted God's protection into 'a land that eats its inhabitants.' The people's crying for no reason became תשעה באב for all generations, and the מרגלים died an unusual death. The גמרא then returns to the crossing of the ירדן, where the ארון carried its own carriers. That miracle explains why עוזא was punished in the time of דוד, and רבא explains that דוד himself was punished for calling תורה 'songs.' The amud ends with the people of בית שמש, who were struck for how they treated the ארון; the explanation of their words continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The spies' going was as wicked as their coming back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחי, learns from the words 'they went and they came' that the מרגלים had an evil plan from the very start of their trip.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'they went and they came.' רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: the פסוק puts the going next to the coming. Just as their coming back was with an evil plan, so too their going out was with an evil plan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about the מרגלים and brings a teaching that they planned evil from the beginning, not only when they returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins 'going' and 'coming' in one breath, so they are compared. We know their return was evil because they brought a bad report. The comparison teaches that the same bad plan was already there when they left.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares; puts two things side by side so one teaches about the other (from הֶקֵּשׁ)
Going; here, the spies setting out
Coming; here, the spies coming back
An evil plan or wicked intention

phrases.english: "And they went and they came."
phrases.notes: במדבר 13:26

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
The verse compares the going to the coming.
Just as the coming back was with an evil plan,
so too the going out was with an evil plan.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַקֵּישׁ הֲלִיכָה לְבִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier explanation of the פסוקים about the מרגלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מרגלים set out with the same evil plan they had when they returned.

steps.title: Why the spies began with praise before slander
steps.stepSummary: The מרגלים first praised the land and then said 'but the people are fierce.' רבי מאיר explains that slander only works if it begins with something true.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'They told him and said: we came to the land... and it flows with milk and honey,' and then it says 'But the people are fierce.' רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי מאיר (a memory aid: truth, alone, borrowing): any לשון הרע that does not start with something true will not be believed in the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the מרגלים praised the land before slandering it, and רבי מאיר explains why they did that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a hidden question: why would people trying to discourage the nation start by praising the land? The answer is that a lie is only believed when it is wrapped in some truth. So the true praise was a tool to make the slander that followed believable.

keyTerms.meaning: But; however; it turns the praise into criticism
A memory aid for remembering a list of teachings
Does not hold up; will not be believed

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how harmful speech often works: a little truth is used to make the falsehood convincing.

phrases.english: "And they told him, and said: We came," etc.
phrases.notes: במדבר 13:27, where they go on to praise the land as flowing with milk and honey.

phrases.english: and it is written: "But the people are fierce."
phrases.notes: במדבר 13:28

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said
(memory aid: truth, alone, borrowing)
phrases.notes: Three code words to help you remember three teachings of רבי מאיר. Only the first one, 'truth', comes here.

phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Meir:
Any slander
that does not have something true at its beginning
will not hold up in the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּל לָשׁוֹן הָרַע שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דְּבַר אֱמֶת בִּתְחִילָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק in the story of the מרגלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slander that does not begin with some truth will not be believed in the end.

steps.title: כלב swayed the people with words
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that 'וַיַּהַס' means כלב swayed the people with his words.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'And כלב quieted the people toward משה.' רבה said: this means he swayed them with words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the word וַיַּהַס, saying כלב quieted the people by persuading them with words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וַיַּהַס is read as connected to הִסִּיתָן, 'he swayed them.' So כלב did not just tell them to be quiet; he used clever words to win them over. The next lines will show how.

keyTerms.meaning: He swayed them; he persuaded them

phrases.english: "And Caleb quieted the people toward Moses."
phrases.notes: במדבר 13:30

phrases.english: Rabbah said: That he swayed them with words.
phrases.notes: וַיַּהַס and הִסִּיתָן sound alike, and רבה reads one as hinting to the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: שֶׁהִסִּיתָן בִּדְבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next פסוק, now about כלב's response to the מרגלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: וַיַּהַס means כלב persuaded the people with his words.

steps.title: The people mock יהושע when he tries to speak
steps.stepSummary: Before כלב spoke, יהושע tried to address the people, but they cut him off with an insult.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהושע began to speak. While he was speaking, they said to him: should this man with a cut-off head speak?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts telling the story behind how כלב swayed the people. This step sets things up: יהושע tries first and is shouted down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people refuse to listen to יהושע and insult him as 'a cut-off head.' This explains why יהושע could not quiet them. It prepares for the next lines, where כלב will use a different approach.

phrases.english: Joshua began to speak.
As he was speaking, they said to him:
Should this one, with a cut-off head, speak?
phrases.notes: They are mocking him for having no children, like a head with nothing coming after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּתַח יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, דְּקָא מִשְׁתַּעֵי אָמְרִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the story explaining how כלב swayed the people, as רבה said in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people refused to listen to יהושע and insulted him, setting the stage for כלב's approach.

steps.title: כלב gets the crowd to go quiet
steps.stepSummary: כלב knows the people will shout him down, so he opens with words that sound like criticism of משה. The crowd goes silent to hear him.
steps.simpleTranslation: כלב said to himself: If I speak normally, they will say something insulting about me and shut me up. So he said to them: 'Is this the only thing the son of עמרם did to us?' They thought he was about to speak against משה, so they became quiet.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues from יהושע being cut off. Now כלב uses a clever opening line so the crowd will let him speak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושע failed because the people silenced him with an insult. כלב avoids this by starting with a line that sounds like he is on their side against משה. This gets their attention and sets up the speech in the next step.

phrases.english: He said [to himself]: If I speak,
phrases.notes: This is כלב thinking to himself, after he saw what happened to יהושע.

phrases.english: they will say something about me and shut me up.
He said to them: And is this the only thing
that the son of Amram did to us?
phrases.notes: That's משה. Calling him just 'son of עמרם' made it sound like כלב was about to complain.

phrases.english: They thought he was speaking to his discredit,
[so] they became silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: אִי מִשְׁתַּעֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: after יהושע was cut off, כלב finds a way to be heard. This explains how the 'וַיַּהַס' of step 3 actually happened.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כלב quieted the crowd by opening with words that sounded like criticism of משה.

steps.title: כלב turns it into praise of משה
steps.stepSummary: Once the crowd is quiet, כלב lists the great things משה did and says that we should follow him even if he told us to climb to heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: He took us out of מצרים, split the sea for us, and fed us the מן. If he told us, 'Build ladders and go up to the sky,' wouldn't we listen to him? 'We will surely go up and take possession of it.'
steps.whatsHappening: כלב flips his opening line. It was not a complaint. He means משה did so much more for us, so we should trust him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gotcha line 'Is this all he did?' now means 'He did far more than this.' כלב argues that after such miracles, going up to the land is easy compared to climbing to heaven. The גמרא reads the פסוק 'עָלֹה נַעֲלֶה' as meaning 'we would go up even to heaven.'

keyTerms.meaning: the food from heaven in the desert

steps.whatToRemember: כלב's trick: he opened with what sounded like criticism, then turned it into full trust in משה.

phrases.english: He said to them: He took us out of Egypt,
and split the sea for us,
and fed us the manna.
If he says, 'Make ladders and go up to the sky,'
would we not listen to him?
'We will surely go up and possess it, etc.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 13:30. 'Go up' is read here as 'go up even to heaven.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הוֹצִיאָנוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes כלב's speech that step 5 set up, turning the seeming criticism into praise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since משה did such great miracles for us, we would follow him even to heaven, and certainly into the land.

steps.title: The מרגלים claim the land's people are 'stronger than Him'
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא reads 'מִמֶּנּוּ' as 'than Him,' meaning the מרגלים claimed that even God could not defeat the Canaanites.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'But the men who went up with him said: We cannot go up, etc.' רבי חנינא בר פפא said: The מרגלים said a terrible thing at that moment. 'For they are stronger מִמֶּנּוּ.' Do not read it as 'than us,' but as 'than Him.' As if to say, even the owner of the house cannot take His belongings out of there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק, where the מרגלים answer כלב. רבי חנינא בר פפא explains why their words were so serious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Hebrew word מִמֶּנּוּ can mean either 'than us' or 'than him.' רבי חנינא בר פפא reads it as 'than Him,' meaning God. So the מרגלים were not only saying the people were too strong for בני ישראל. They were claiming the Canaanites were too strong for God Himself, the 'owner' of the land.

keyTerms.meaning: do not read it as (a way of reading a word differently)
as if it could be said (used when speaking about God)
the owner of the house, here meaning God

steps.confusionAlert: The written word does not change. מִמֶּנּוּ can honestly mean 'than us' or 'than him.' The גמרא is choosing the second meaning to show how bad the words of the מרגלים were.

phrases.english: 'But the men that went up with him
phrases.notes: במדבר 13:31

phrases.english: said: We are not able, etc.'
Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר גָּדוֹל דִּבְּרוּ מְרַגְּלִים בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה.
phrases.english: The spies said a terrible thing at that moment.
'For they are stronger mimmennu,'
do not read 'than us,'
but rather 'than Him,'
phrases.notes: Both readings come from the same Hebrew word; only the meaning changes.

phrases.english: as it were, even the owner of the house
is unable to remove His belongings from there.
phrases.notes: The 'owner' is הקדוש ברוך הוא, and the 'belongings' are the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא: דָּבָר גָּדוֹל דִּבְּרוּ מְרַגְּלִים בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק, the answer of the מרגלים to כלב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מרגלים claimed the Canaanites were stronger than God Himself.

steps.title: God meant the deaths for good, but the מרגלים saw it as bad
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains 'a land that eats its people': God made important Canaanites die wherever the מרגלים went, so the locals would be too busy to notice them. The מרגלים twisted this into a bad report.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It is a land that eats up its inhabitants.' רבא taught: הקדוש ברוך הוא said: I meant it for good, but they took it as bad. I meant it for good: wherever they came, the important person of that place died, so that the people would be busy and would not ask about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next complaint of the מרגלים, that the land 'eats its inhabitants.' רבא shows that what they saw was really a kindness from God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מרגלים saw funerals everywhere and concluded that the land kills people. רבא says God caused those deaths on purpose so the Canaanites would be busy mourning and would not question the strangers. So the protection was real, but the מרגלים turned it into slander.

keyTerms.meaning: a land that eats up its inhabitants

phrases.english: 'It is a land that eats up its inhabitants,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 13:32

phrases.aramaic: דָּרֵשׁ רָבָא, אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Rava taught: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
I intended it for good,
but they took it as bad.
I intended it for good:
that anywhere they arrived,
the important one of them died,
phrases.notes: 'Of them' means the important person among the Canaanites of that place.

phrases.english: so that they would be busy
and not ask about them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רָבָא, אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: אֲנִי חֲשַׁבְתִּיהָ לְטוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next words of the מרגלים in the פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The deaths the מרגלים saw were God's way of protecting them, but they turned it into a bad report.

steps.title: Another version: the death of איוב
steps.stepSummary: A second version says that איוב died at that time, and everyone was busy with his funeral. The מרגלים still turned this into 'a land that eats its inhabitants.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: איוב died, and everyone was busy with his eulogy. They took it as bad: 'It is a land that eats up its inhabitants.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of how God kept the Canaanites busy. This time it was one big funeral, for איוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main idea stays the same: God sent a distraction to protect the מרגלים, and they twisted it. Only the detail changes. In this version it was not many important people dying in each place, but the death of איוב, which kept the whole world busy mourning.
steps.whatToRemember: Whether it was many deaths or the death of איוב, God sent it to protect the מרגלים. They turned God's kindness into slander about the land.

phrases.english: And some say: Job died,
and the whole world was busy with his eulogy,
[yet] they took it as bad:
'It is a land that eats up its inhabitants.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אִיּוֹב נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the distraction described in step 8. The main point, that God meant it for good, stays the same.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The distraction was the funeral of איוב, which the מרגלים also turned into a bad report.

steps.title: רב משרשיא: The מרגלים Lied About the Grasshoppers
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא says the מרגלים were liars. They could say they felt like grasshoppers, but how could they know what the Canaanites thought of them?
steps.simpleTranslation: The מרגלים said: 'We were like grasshoppers in our own eyes, and so were we in their eyes.' רב משרשיא said: The מרגלים were liars. It makes sense that they could say 'we felt like grasshoppers in our own eyes.' But 'so were we in their eyes': how could they have known that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line from the מרגלים' report, and רב משרשיא claims part of it must be a lie.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two halves. The first half describes the מרגלים' own feelings, which they could know. The second half claims to know what the Canaanites were thinking, and רב משרשיא argues they had no way to know that, so they made it up.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense that... (used to accept one part before questioning another)

phrases.english: "And we were like grasshoppers in our own eyes, and so were we," etc.
phrases.notes: במדבר 13:33. The full פסוק ends 'in their eyes', meaning in the Canaanites' eyes.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said:
The spies were liars.
Granted, "we were like grasshoppers in our own eyes" is fine,
but "and so were we in their eyes":
from where could they have known that?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: מְרַגְּלִים שַׁקָּרֵי הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the reading of the מרגלים' report, moving to the next phrase in the פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The claim 'so were we in their eyes' was a lie, because the מרגלים could not have known what the Canaanites thought.

steps.title: They Really Did Overhear the Canaanites
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב משרשיא's claim: the מרגלים hid in trees at a Canaanite mourners' meal and heard them say they saw grasshopper-like people in the trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. When the Canaanites held the mourners' meal, they held it under cedar trees. When the מרגלים saw them, they climbed up and sat in the trees. They heard the Canaanites saying: 'We see people who look like grasshoppers in the trees.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב משרשיא and shows how the מרגלים could have known what the Canaanites thought of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב משרשיא's whole argument was 'they had no way to know.' The גמרא answers by giving them a way: they heard it with their own ears while hiding in the trees. This connects to Step 8, where God caused important Canaanites to die, which is why there was a mourners' meal at all.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not so (the גמרא rejecting a claim)
Serving the meal given to mourners after a death

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the מרגלים were honest people in general. It only defends this one claim: they really did hear the Canaanites call them grasshoppers.

phrases.english: But that is not so,
for when they were holding the mourners' meal,
phrases.notes: 'They' here means the Canaanites, mourning the people who died while the מרגלים were there.

phrases.english: they would hold the meal under cedar trees.
And when the spies saw them, they climbed up and sat in the trees.
They heard them saying:
"We see people who look like grasshoppers in the trees."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the claim of Step 10 that the מרגלים lied about how the Canaanites saw them.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב משרשיא's claim that the second half of the פסוק was a lie.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב משרשיא assumed the מרגלים had no way of knowing the Canaanites' view, but they overheard it directly from the trees.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'grasshoppers' line was not made up. The מרגלים heard the Canaanites say it while hiding in the trees at the mourners' meal.

steps.title: The Crying for No Reason Became תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: רבה in the name of רבי יוחנן: the night the people cried was the eve of תשעה באב. Since they cried for nothing, God set that day as a day of crying for all generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And all the congregation lifted up their voice and cried.' רבה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: That day was the eve of תשעה באב. הקדוש ברוך הוא said: They cried a crying for no reason, and I will set up for them a crying for all generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the people's reaction to the report and connects their crying to the date of תשעה באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people cried even though nothing bad had happened. Their crying was based only on the false report. As a measure-for-measure response, God made that same date a day of real tragedy and crying for the future.

keyTerms.meaning: The eve of the Ninth of אב
Crying for nothing, with no real reason

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a root reason for why תשעה באב became the Jewish day of mourning: it began with the crying over the מרגלים' report.

phrases.aramaic: ״וַתִּשָּׂא כׇּל הָעֵדָה וַיִּתְּנוּ אֶת קוֹלָם וַיִּבְכּוּ״,
phrases.english: "And all the congregation lifted up and gave their voice, and they cried."
phrases.notes: במדבר 14:1

phrases.english: Rabba said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם עֶרֶב תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב הָיָה,
phrases.english: That day was the eve of the Ninth of Av.
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
They cried a crying for no reason,
so I will set up for them a crying for the generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם עֶרֶב תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves forward in the story from the מרגלים' report to the people's crying reaction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The crying over the report was on the eve of תשעה באב, and because it was for no reason, God made that date a day of crying for all generations.

steps.title: The People Threw Stones Upward
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא reads two parts of the same פסוק together: the people wanted to stone, and God's glory appeared. He learns that they threw stones upward, as if at God.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And all the congregation said to stone them with stones,' and it is written right after: 'And the glory of ה׳ appeared in the אהל מועד.' רבי חייא בר אבא said: This teaches that they took stones and threw them upward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the people's anger getting worse, from crying to throwing stones, and reads the פסוק to show who they were really aiming at.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא בר אבא connects the two halves of the פסוק. Right where it talks about stoning, it mentions God's glory appearing. From this closeness he learns that the stones were thrown upward, toward God Himself.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches (introduces a lesson learned from a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: The rebellion grew step by step: a false report, crying for nothing (which became תשעה באב), and finally stones thrown upward, as if at God.

phrases.english: "And all the congregation said to stone them with stones,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 14:10

phrases.english: and it is written: "And the glory of the Lord appeared in the Tent of Meeting."
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק, right after the words about stoning.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said:
This teaches that they took stones
and threw them upward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁנָּטְלוּ אֲבָנִים וּזְרָקוּם כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after the crying and shows the people's reaction growing more extreme.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading the two halves of the פסוק together teaches that the people threw stones upward, as if against God.

steps.title: The spies died an unusual death
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק about the מרגלים dying 'in the plague,' ריש לקיש says they died a strange, unusual death.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the men who brought out an evil report of the land died by the plague.' רבי שמעון בן לקיש says: this means they died an unusual death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about how the מרגלים died. רבי שמעון בן לקיש explains that their death was not normal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said 'they died.' Adding 'by the plague' tells רבי שמעון בן לקיש that their death was special and unusual. This sets up the next two opinions, which describe what that death looked like.

keyTerms.meaning: the bad report about the land

phrases.english: "And the men who brought out the report of the land
phrases.notes: במדבר 14:37

phrases.english: as evil, died by the plague"
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
That they died an unusual death.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיָּמֻתוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים מוֹצִאֵי דִבַּת הָאָרֶץ רָעָה בַּמַּגֵּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the מרגלים by telling how they were punished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מרגלים died a strange, unusual death.

steps.title: Their tongues stretched down and worms crawled through
steps.stepSummary: רבי שילא, quoted by רבי חנינא בר פפא, describes the unusual death: their tongues stretched to their navels, and worms crawled back and forth between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר פפא said that רבי שילא of כפר תמרתא taught: their tongues stretched out and fell onto their navels. Worms came out of their tongues and went into their navels, and came out of their navels and went into their tongues.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a picture of what the 'unusual death' of the מרגלים was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishment matches the sin. They sinned with their tongues by speaking badly about the land, so their tongues were punished in a disgusting and painful way.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa said,

phrases.aramaic: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי שֵׁילָא אִישׁ כְּפַר תְּמַרְתָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Sheila of the village of Temarta taught:
This teaches that their tongues stretched out
and fell onto their navels,
and worms were coming out of their tongues
and going into their navels,
and from their navels and going into their tongues.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי שֵׁילָא אִישׁ כְּפַר תְּמַרְתָּא מְלַמֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in what the 'unusual death' from step 14 was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מרגלים died with stretched tongues and worms moving between tongue and navel.

steps.title: Another view: they died of choking sickness
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the מרגלים died of אסכרה, a sickness of the throat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן בר יצחק said: they died of אסכרה, a choking sickness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different opinion about how the מרגלים died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק also links the death to the mouth and throat, the place where their sin of bad speech came from. He just names a different illness than רבי שילא did.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון בן לקיש says only that the מרגלים died an unusual death. רבי שילא and רב נחמן בר יצחק each describe that death, and both descriptions involve the tongue or throat, the organs they used for their bad speech.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
They died of a choking sickness (askara).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different description from step 15 of the unusual death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מרגלים died of אסכרה.

steps.title: When the last Jew left the Jordan, the water came back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the crossing of the ירדן: as soon as the last Jew came up out of the river, the water flowed back, as the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the last Jew came up out of the ירדן, the water returned to its place. As the פסוק says: 'When the כהנים carrying the ארון came up out of the ירדן, and their feet touched dry land, the water of the ירדן returned to its place and flowed over its banks like before.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story of בני ישראל crossing the ירדן. It says the water came back right when the crossing ended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ties the water's return to the moment the כהנים carrying the ארון stepped out. That means they stood in the river until all the people crossed, and only then stepped back out on the side they came from. This sets up the next step, where the ארון is left on the wrong side.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵיוָן שֶׁעָלָה הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מִן הַיַּרְדֵּן
phrases.english: And once the last of the Jewish people came up out of the Jordan
the water returned to its place,
as it says: "And it was, when the priests came up,
phrases.notes: יהושע 4:18

phrases.aramaic: נֹשְׂאֵי אֲרוֹן בְּרִית ה׳ מִתּוֹךְ הַיַּרְדֵּן
phrases.english: those carrying the Ark of the covenant of God, out of the middle of the Jordan,

phrases.aramaic: נִתְּקוּ כַּפּוֹת רַגְלֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים אֶל הֶחָרָבָה
phrases.english: the soles of the priests' feet were pulled up onto the dry land,
and the water of the Jordan returned to its place

phrases.aramaic: וַיֵּלְכוּ כִתְמוֹל שִׁלְשׁוֹם עַל כׇּל גְּדוֹתָיו״,
phrases.english: and flowed as it did before, over all its banks."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן שֶׁעָלָה הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מִן הַיַּרְדֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the מרגלים story and returns to the earlier story of crossing the ירדן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The water of the ירדן returned only after the last Jew came out, when the כהנים carrying the ארון stepped out.

steps.title: The ארון carried its carriers across
steps.stepSummary: Since the ארון and its carriers were left on one side and the people on the other, the ארון lifted its carriers and crossed over by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the ארון, its carriers, and the כהנים were on one side, and the Jewish people were on the other side. The ארון carried its carriers and crossed, as the פסוק says: 'When all the people finished crossing, the ארון of God and the כהנים crossed before the people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the last step: the ארון was stuck on the far side, so it crossed in a miraculous way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water had already returned, so the כהנים could not walk across. The פסוק still says the ארון and the כהנים crossed after everyone, so the גמרא learns that the ארון lifted its own carriers and brought them over.
steps.confusionAlert: Normally the כהנים carry the ארון. Here it is the opposite: the ארון carried the כהנים.

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא אָרוֹן וְנוֹשְׂאָיו וְכֹהֲנִים מִצַּד אֶחָד,
phrases.english: It turns out that the Ark, its carriers, and the priests were on one side,
and the Jewish people were on the other side.
The Ark carried its carriers and crossed,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיְהִי כַּאֲשֶׁר תַּם כׇּל הָעָם לַעֲבֹר
phrases.english: as it says: "And it was, when all the people had finished crossing,
phrases.notes: יהושע 4:11

phrases.aramaic: וַיַּעֲבֹר אֲרוֹן ה׳ וְהַכֹּהֲנִים לִפְנֵי הָעָם״.
phrases.english: the Ark of God and the priests crossed before the people."

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצָא אָרוֹן וְנוֹשְׂאָיו וְכֹהֲנִים מִצַּד אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 17: since the water already returned, the ארון had to cross by a miracle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ארון miraculously carried its carriers across the ירדן.

steps.title: Why עוזא was punished for grabbing the ארון
steps.stepSummary: Because the ארון once carried its carriers, עוזא was punished for grabbing it to stop it from falling: surely it could hold itself up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of this, עוזא was punished, as the פסוק says: 'They came to the threshing floor of כידן, and עוזא reached out his hand to hold the ארון.' The הקדוש ברוך הוא said to him: עוזא, the ארון carried its carriers. Surely it can carry itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the miracle from the last step to explain a later story, the punishment of עוזא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עוזא grabbed the ארון because he was afraid it would fall. God's answer is a קל וחומר: if the ארון could lift the people carrying it, it surely does not need help holding itself up. Grabbing it showed he did not treat the ארון with proper understanding.

keyTerms.meaning: all the more so (a קל וחומר)

steps.whatToRemember: The ארון carried its own carriers across the ירדן. So עוזא should have known it did not need his help, and that is why he was punished.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties two far-apart stories together: a miracle in יהושע explains a punishment in the time of דוד.

phrases.english: And because of this matter Uzza was punished,
phrases.notes: 'This matter' is the miracle we just learned, the ארון carrying its carriers.

phrases.english: as it says: "And they came to the threshing floor of Kidon,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 13:9

phrases.aramaic: וַיִּשְׁלַח עֻזָּא אֶת יָדוֹ לֶאֱחֹז אֶת הָאָרוֹן״,
phrases.english: and Uzza put out his hand to hold the Ark."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: עוּזָּא,
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him: Uzza,
it carried its carriers,
all the more so itself!
phrases.notes: He means: surely the ארון can hold itself up without your help.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה נֶעֱנַשׁ עוּזָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the miracle from step 18 to explain why עוזא was punished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עוזא was punished because, by קל וחומר, the ארון that carried its carriers could surely hold itself up.

steps.title: Two opinions on why עוזא was struck
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר disagree about the meaning of the word השל. One says it means עוזא's forgetfulness. The other says it means he relieved himself in front of the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says ה׳ struck עוזא 'על השל'. One אמורא says this means he was punished for forgetting. The other says it means he relieved himself in front of the ארון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about עוזא's punishment. Two אמוראים then give different explanations of the unusual word השל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion connects השל to שלו, meaning 'his forgetfulness.' עוזא forgot that the ארון can carry itself, as we saw in step 19. The second opinion reads the word as describing a disrespectful act he did in the ארון's presence.

keyTerms.meaning: An unusual word in the פסוק explaining why עוזא was struck
One says (used when two named Sages disagree and we are not told who said which opinion)

phrases.english: "And the anger of ה׳ burned against Uzza,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 6:7

phrases.english: and He struck him there for the 'shal,' etc."
Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar disagree:
One says: it was because of his forgetfulness.
phrases.notes: He forgot that the ארון can carry itself, as we just learned.

phrases.english: And one says: it was because he relieved himself in front of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the עוזא story from step 19 by explaining the פסוק that describes his punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עוזא was struck either for forgetting that the ארון carries itself, or for relieving himself in front of the ארון.

steps.title: עוזא still came to עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns from the words 'with the ארון of God' that עוזא came to עולם הבא. Just as the ארון lasts forever, so does עוזא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says עוזא died 'with the ארון of God.' רבי יוחנן says this teaches that עוזא came to עולם הבא. Just as the ארון lasts forever, so too עוזא has a place in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן reads the next words of the same פסוק. He uses them to teach that עוזא was not lost forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'with' links עוזא to the ארון. The ארון is something that lasts forever, so the פסוק hints that עוזא also lasts forever, in עולם הבא. Even though he was punished, his final reward was not taken away.

phrases.english: "And he died there with the Ark of God."
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, שמואל ב 6:7

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
Uzza came to the World to Come,
as it says: "with the Ark of God."
Just as the Ark lasts forever,
so too Uzza came to the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: עוּזָּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next words of the same פסוק and explains what happened to עוזא after his death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עוזא came to עולם הבא, which is learned from the comparison to the eternal ארון.

steps.title: דוד's face darkened like a burnt loaf
steps.stepSummary: On the words 'ויחר לדוד,' רבי אלעזר explains that דוד's face changed and darkened like a חררה, a loaf baked on coals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'ויחר לדוד' because ה׳ broke out against עוזא. רבי אלעזר says this means דוד's face changed color like a burnt loaf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next פסוק about how דוד reacted to עוזא's death. רבי אלעזר explains the word ויחר as a change in דוד's face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר connects ויחר to חררה, a loaf that turns dark from the coals. So he reads the word as 'דוד's face darkened from distress,' not 'דוד became angry.' This reading sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'it burned'; usually means anger or being upset
Broke out with a breach (struck suddenly)
A loaf baked on hot coals, which turns dark

phrases.english: "And it burned for David"
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 6:8

phrases.aramaic: עַל אֲשֶׁר פָּרַץ ה׳ פֶּרֶץ בְּעֻזָּה״,
phrases.english: because ה׳ had broken out against Uzza.
Rabbi Elazar says:
It means that his face changed like a loaf baked on coals.
phrases.notes: He hears 'ויחר' as sounding like 'חררה', a dark, coal-baked loaf.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּנּוּ פָּנָיו כַּחֲרָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק, which describes דוד's reaction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this פסוק, ויחר means דוד's face darkened like a חררה.

steps.title: Does every 'ויחר' mean a darkened face?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר. If ויחר means a darkened face, should every place in the תורה that says ויחר be read the same way?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that is so, wherever ויחר is written, should it also mean this?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אלעזר's reading. It asks whether his explanation would have to apply to every ויחר in the תנ״ך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ויחר appears in many places, including the פסוק just before this one about ה׳. A darkened face cannot describe ה׳. So if רבי אלעזר's reading applied everywhere, it would not work.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (introduces a challenge that takes an idea to its logical end)

phrases.english: But if so,
anywhere that 'vayichar' is written,
does it mean this too?!
phrases.notes: That would include the פסוק right before this one, which says 'ויחר' about ה׳ himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה כׇּל הֵיכָא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אלעזר's reading from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's reading of ויחר as a darkened face
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ויחר means a darkened face, the same meaning would have to apply to every ויחר, including ones that describe ה׳, and that cannot be.

steps.title: The word אף makes the difference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that where the פסוק says 'ויחר אף,' it means anger. Here the word אף is missing, so ויחר can mean a darkened face.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the word אף is written. Here, אף is not written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אלעזר. It points out that the two פסוקים use different wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: About ה׳, the פסוק says 'ויחר אף,' and the word אף (anger) shows that the פסוק means anger. About דוד, the פסוק says only 'ויחר' without אף. That leaves room for רבי אלעזר to read it as a darkened face.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's reading only applies where ויחר appears alone. When the פסוק says 'ויחר אף,' it simply means anger.

phrases.english: There, 'af' (anger) is written,
phrases.notes: "There" is the פסוק about ה׳: 'ויחר אף ה׳ בעזה.'

phrases.english: here, 'af' is not written.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם כְּתִיב ״אַף״, הָכָא לָא כְּתִיב ״אַף״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between the cases based on the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every ויחר would have to mean a darkened face, even when it describes ה׳.
steps.terutzMaskana: When ויחר appears with אף, it means anger. When ויחר appears alone, as with דוד, it can mean a darkened face.

steps.title: רבא: דוד was punished for calling תורה 'songs'
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that דוד was punished because he called the words of תורה 'זמירות', songs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: Why was דוד punished? Because he called the words of תורה 'songs,' as it says: 'Your laws were songs to me in the house where I lived.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new teaching. It explains the deeper reason why דוד was punished in the story of עוזא and the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps explained עוזא's own sin. Now רבא asks why דוד deserved this tragedy at all. His answer points to a verse in תהלים where דוד calls the תורה's laws 'songs.'

keyTerms.meaning: Taught or explained, usually by drawing a lesson from a פסוק

phrases.english: Rava taught:
For what reason was David punished?
phrases.notes: He means the punishment of עוזא dying while דוד was bringing the ארון.

phrases.english: Because he called words of Torah "songs,"
as it says: "Your laws were songs to me
in the house where I lived."
phrases.notes: תהלים 119:54

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רָבָא: מִפְּנֵי מָה נֶעֱנַשׁ דָּוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from עוזא and דוד's reaction to the root cause of the whole tragedy
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד was punished because he called the words of תורה 'songs.'

steps.title: God's response: דוד forgets a simple law and carries the ארון on a wagon
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא tells דוד that תורה is hard to hold onto, not light like a song. As a punishment, He makes דוד forget a basic law: the ארון must be carried on the shoulders, not on a wagon.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to him: About the words of תורה it is written, 'Look away from it for a moment and it is gone.' And you call them songs?! I will make you stumble on something that even small schoolchildren know. As it is written: 'But to the sons of קהת he gave no wagons, because the holy work was theirs, and they carried it on their shoulders.' And דוד brought the ארון on a wagon.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues his teaching. He describes how הקדוש ברוך הוא answered דוד and how the punishment fit the sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תורה is so easy to forget that it cannot be treated lightly, like a song. So the punishment was measure for measure. דוד forgot an easy law, that the ארון is carried on the shoulders, and put it on a wagon. That mistake led to the tragedy with עוזא.

steps.whatToRemember: דוד treated תורה lightly by calling it 'songs.' So he was made to forget a simple law, and he brought the ארון on a wagon instead of on people's shoulders.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the ארון was on a wagon at all. That wagon set up the whole עוזא story.

steps.title: Why were the people of בית שמש struck just for looking?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about the people of בית שמש being struck 'because they looked at the ארון.' It asks: could just looking really deserve such a punishment?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And He struck the men of בית שמש because they looked at the ארון.' Just because they looked, God struck them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a different ארון story from the days of שמואל. It asks a question that sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק makes it sound like only looking at the ארון caused the punishment. That seems too harsh. So the גמרא suggests they must have done something more serious, and the next step explains what it was.

steps.title: רבי אבהו and רבי אלעזר explain the real sin of בית שמש
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו and רבי אלעזר disagree. One says the people bowed to the ארון while they kept on harvesting. The other says they also spoke words, meaning disrespectful words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו and רבי אלעזר disagreed. One said: they were harvesting and bowing at the same time. The other said: they also said words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with two opinions. Both explain that 'looking' really means a disrespectful way of treating the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the first opinion, they did not stop their work in honor of the ארון. They bowed while they kept harvesting, which showed a lack of respect. By the second opinion, they also said words against it. The next lines of the גמרא explain what those words were.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu and Rabbi Elazar disagreed:
One said: they were harvesting and bowing down at the same time,
and one said: they also said words.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about why looking at the ארון was punished
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They showed disrespect to the ארון. By one opinion, they bowed while still harvesting. By the other, they also spoke disrespectful words.
